title: Cell Specialization and Microscopy Evidence Core Test
description: Use microscope evidence, models, and structure-function reasoning to explain specialized cells.

questions.prompt: A microscope image shows flat cells lining a surface and long cells that can contract. Which idea best explains the different shapes?
questions.questionText: A microscope image shows flat cells lining a surface and long cells that can contract. Which idea best explains the different shapes?
options: Cell structure is related to cell function.
All cells must have the same shape.
Cell shape is never useful evidence.
Only nonliving things have structures.
questions.correctAnswer: Cell structure is related to cell function.
questions.explanation: Different cell shapes can support different jobs.

questions.prompt: Which observation is strongest evidence that a tissue is made of specialized cells?
questions.questionText: Which observation is strongest evidence that a tissue is made of specialized cells?
options: The tissue is placed near a window.
The cells have similar shapes and work together for one function.
The sample is labeled with a marker.
The slide has a clear cover.
questions.correctAnswer: The cells have similar shapes and work together for one function.
questions.explanation: A tissue is made of similar specialized cells that work together.

questions.prompt: A nerve cell has long branches. Which function does this structure most likely support?
questions.questionText: A nerve cell has long branches. Which function does this structure most likely support?
options: storing sunlight
making a stiff cell wall
sending signals over distance
turning into a mineral
questions.correctAnswer: sending signals over distance
questions.explanation: Long branches help nerve cells connect and send signals.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows the relationship among cells, tissues, and organs?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows the relationship among cells, tissues, and organs?
options: organs -> sunlight -> no cells
tissues -> rocks -> organisms
cells -> no organization -> organ system
specialized cells -> tissues -> organs with larger functions
questions.correctAnswer: specialized cells -> tissues -> organs with larger functions
questions.explanation: Specialized cells form tissues, and tissues form organs.

questions.prompt: A student says, "All cells in the body do the same job." Which evidence best challenges that claim?
questions.questionText: A student says, "All cells in the body do the same job." Which evidence best challenges that claim?
options: Muscle cells contract, while nerve cells carry signals.
All cells are very small.
Many cells have membranes.
Cells can be viewed with microscopes.
questions.correctAnswer: Muscle cells contract, while nerve cells carry signals.
questions.explanation: Different specialized cells perform different jobs.

questions.prompt: A cell has many mitochondria compared with nearby cells. Which inference is most reasonable?
questions.questionText: A cell has many mitochondria compared with nearby cells. Which inference is most reasonable?
options: The cell cannot use energy.
The cell may need a lot of usable energy for its work.
The cell is definitely nonliving.
The cell has no membrane.
questions.correctAnswer: The cell may need a lot of usable energy for its work.
questions.explanation: More mitochondria can support higher energy needs.

questions.prompt: A model of a leaf shows many cells with chloroplasts near the surface. What does this arrangement help explain?
questions.questionText: A model of a leaf shows many cells with chloroplasts near the surface. What does this arrangement help explain?
options: why leaves do not contain cells
why chloroplasts are found only in animals
how leaf structure supports photosynthesis
why plants never need light
questions.correctAnswer: how leaf structure supports photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Leaf cells with chloroplasts near light can support sugar production.

questions.prompt: Which investigation best tests whether a microscope model is accurate?
questions.questionText: Which investigation best tests whether a microscope model is accurate?
options: Choose the prettiest drawing.
Ask whether the drawing uses green ink.
Ignore the slide and use only memory.
Compare the drawing with several clear microscope observations.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare the drawing with several clear microscope observations.
questions.explanation: Models should be checked against evidence.

questions.prompt: A blood sample has many small cells shaped to move through narrow vessels. Which statement best connects structure and function?
questions.questionText: A blood sample has many small cells shaped to move through narrow vessels. Which statement best connects structure and function?
options: The shape helps the cells travel and exchange materials efficiently.
The shape proves the cells are not living.
The cells are organs.
The shape prevents all movement.
questions.correctAnswer: The shape helps the cells travel and exchange materials efficiently.
questions.explanation: Cell structure can support the job the cell performs.

questions.prompt: A student labels a diagram: cells -> organs -> tissues -> organ systems. What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student labels a diagram: cells -> organs -> tissues -> organ systems. What is the best correction?
options: Cells should be removed.
Tissues should come before organs.
Organ systems should come before cells.
Tissues are larger than organ systems.
questions.correctAnswer: Tissues should come before organs.
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form organ systems.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would support that a cell is specialized for absorbing materials?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would support that a cell is specialized for absorbing materials?
options: It is drawn with a thick border.
It is named Cell A.
It has a folded surface that increases contact area.
It is next to a ruler.
questions.correctAnswer: It has a folded surface that increases contact area.
questions.explanation: A folded surface can increase area for absorption.

questions.prompt: Why is a tissue not the same thing as one cell?
questions.questionText: Why is a tissue not the same thing as one cell?
options: A tissue is always nonliving.
A tissue contains no cells.
A tissue is smaller than a single molecule.
A tissue is a group of cells working together.
questions.correctAnswer: A tissue is a group of cells working together.
questions.explanation: Tissues are made of cells with related functions.

questions.prompt: A scientist sees cells arranged in tight layers with few gaps. Which function might this structure support?
questions.questionText: A scientist sees cells arranged in tight layers with few gaps. Which function might this structure support?
options: forming a protective barrier
carrying nerve signals across a body
making sunlight
breaking rocks into sand
questions.correctAnswer: forming a protective barrier
questions.explanation: Tightly packed cells can help create a barrier.

questions.prompt: Which question would best deepen a model of cell specialization?
questions.questionText: Which question would best deepen a model of cell specialization?
options: What color is the model title?
How does each cell structure help the cell's specific job?
Can the diagram be made larger?
How many letters are in the cell name?
questions.correctAnswer: How does each cell structure help the cell's specific job?
questions.explanation: A strong model connects structures to functions.

questions.prompt: A slide is blurry, and a student claims the cells have no nucleus. What is the best response?
questions.questionText: A slide is blurry, and a student claims the cells have no nucleus. What is the best response?
options: Accept the claim because blurry evidence is strongest.
Throw out all microscope evidence forever.
Improve the observation before using it as evidence.
Decide that all cells lack nuclei.
questions.correctAnswer: Improve the observation before using it as evidence.
questions.explanation: Poor observations should not support strong claims.

questions.prompt: A plant root cell has a long extension into soil. Which function does that structure likely support?
questions.questionText: A plant root cell has a long extension into soil. Which function does that structure likely support?
options: detecting sound
making a bone
storing memories
absorbing water and minerals
questions.correctAnswer: absorbing water and minerals
questions.explanation: Root extensions increase contact with soil for absorption.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why specialization matters in multicellular organisms?
questions.questionText: Which statement best explains why specialization matters in multicellular organisms?
options: Different cell types do different jobs that help the whole organism function.
Every cell doing the same job is always more efficient.
Specialization means cells stop working together.
Only single-celled organisms have specialized cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Different cell types do different jobs that help the whole organism function.
questions.explanation: Specialization supports complex body functions.

questions.prompt: A model leaves out interactions among cell types in an organ. What weakness does the model have?
questions.questionText: A model leaves out interactions among cell types in an organ. What weakness does the model have?
options: It has too much evidence.
It may show parts but miss how the organ works as a system.
It proves organs are nonliving.
It explains all functions perfectly.
questions.correctAnswer: It may show parts but miss how the organ works as a system.
questions.explanation: Organs work through interactions among tissues and cells.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern would support a structure-function claim?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern would support a structure-function claim?
options: All slides were stored in the same drawer.
The microscope was black.
Cells with more folded surface absorb dye faster than cells with smooth surfaces.
The labels used capital letters.
questions.correctAnswer: Cells with more folded surface absorb dye faster than cells with smooth surfaces.
questions.explanation: The pattern links a structure difference to a function difference.

questions.prompt: A student says, "If cells are specialized, they cannot depend on other cells." Which correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student says, "If cells are specialized, they cannot depend on other cells." Which correction is best?
options: Specialized cells are independent organisms.
Specialization removes the need for systems.
Cells in tissues never interact.
Specialized cells still work with other cells in tissues and organs.
questions.correctAnswer: Specialized cells still work with other cells in tissues and organs.
questions.explanation: Specialized cells depend on larger systems.

questions.prompt: Which model best connects this concept to body systems?
questions.questionText: Which model best connects this concept to body systems?
options: specialized cells -> tissues -> organs -> interacting organ systems
cells -> no tissues -> no organs -> no body
organ systems -> single cell only
rocks -> tissues -> organs
questions.correctAnswer: specialized cells -> tissues -> organs -> interacting organ systems
questions.explanation: This sequence links cell specialization to body organization.

questions.prompt: A cell is shaped like a flat tile and found in a sheet. Which claim is strongest?
questions.questionText: A cell is shaped like a flat tile and found in a sheet. Which claim is strongest?
options: The cell must store all body energy.
The cell may help cover or line a surface.
The cell cannot be living.
The cell must be a whole organ.
questions.correctAnswer: The cell may help cover or line a surface.
questions.explanation: Flat cells in sheets often support lining or covering functions.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would weaken a claim that all cells in a sample have the same function?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would weaken a claim that all cells in a sample have the same function?
options: The slide is rectangular.
The microscope has a light.
The sample contains cells with very different shapes and structures.
The sample name is written neatly.
questions.correctAnswer: The sample contains cells with very different shapes and structures.
questions.explanation: Different shapes and structures can suggest different functions.

questions.prompt: A student compares cells to tools in a toolbox. Which part of the analogy is strongest?
questions.questionText: A student compares cells to tools in a toolbox. Which part of the analogy is strongest?
options: Tools and cells are both nonliving.
All tools do the same job.
A toolbox is an organ system.
Different tools have structures suited to different jobs, like specialized cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Different tools have structures suited to different jobs, like specialized cells.
questions.explanation: The useful part of the analogy is structure matched to job.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best links microscope evidence to a claim about living systems?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best links microscope evidence to a claim about living systems?
options: Microscope observations reveal cells, and cell structures can show how living systems perform functions.
Microscopes replace the need for reasoning.
Any blurry picture proves a claim.
Cells are unrelated to living systems.
questions.correctAnswer: Microscope observations reveal cells, and cell structures can show how living systems perform functions.
questions.explanation: Microscope evidence can support claims when interpreted carefully.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows a muscle tissue with parallel fibers. Which function is best supported?
questions.questionText: A diagram shows a muscle tissue with parallel fibers. Which function is best supported?
options: photosynthesis
coordinated contraction
filtering light into colors
storing rocks
questions.correctAnswer: coordinated contraction
questions.explanation: Parallel muscle fibers can support coordinated contraction.

questions.prompt: What makes an explanation stronger than a label in a cell diagram?
questions.questionText: What makes an explanation stronger than a label in a cell diagram?
options: It uses more colors only.
It avoids mentioning function.
It connects the labeled structure to evidence and function.
It replaces evidence with guesses.
questions.correctAnswer: It connects the labeled structure to evidence and function.
questions.explanation: Science explanations need relationships, not labels alone.

questions.prompt: A student claims a cell with many chloroplasts is from a plant surface receiving light. Which evidence would strengthen the claim?
questions.questionText: A student claims a cell with many chloroplasts is from a plant surface receiving light. Which evidence would strengthen the claim?
options: The cell was drawn in pencil.
The slide is next to a notebook.
The microscope lens is round.
The cell is in leaf tissue and near a light-exposed surface.
questions.correctAnswer: The cell is in leaf tissue and near a light-exposed surface.
questions.explanation: Location and chloroplast evidence together support the claim.

questions.prompt: Which final explanation best shows understanding of cell specialization?
questions.questionText: Which final explanation best shows understanding of cell specialization?
options: Cell structures provide evidence about function, and specialized cells work together in tissues, organs, and systems.
All cells do the same job.
Microscope labels are stronger than evidence.
Tissues are unrelated to cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Cell structures provide evidence about function, and specialized cells work together in tissues, organs, and systems.
questions.explanation: This connects evidence, structure, function, and levels of organization.

questions.prompt: Which question would make a student think beyond memorizing cell parts?
questions.questionText: Which question would make a student think beyond memorizing cell parts?
options: What is the first letter of the structure name?
How would the cell's job be affected if this structure were missing or changed?
Is the diagram printed in color?
Can the word cell be spelled backward?
questions.correctAnswer: How would the cell's job be affected if this structure were missing or changed?
questions.explanation: Changing a structure asks the student to reason about function.
